nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and all vertices $x$ and $y$ of the complete graph $K_n$, whose vertices are the natural numbers less than $n$, $x$ and $y$ are adjacent if and only if $x \ne y$.
nodes.title: Adjacency in the complete graph

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $K_n$ is the finite graph whose vertices are the natural numbers less than $n$, in which any two distinct vertices are adjacent.
nodes.title: Complete graph as a finite graph

nodes.summary: A finite graph consists of a finite vertex set $V$ together with a simple graph on $V$, that is, a symmetric and irreflexive adjacency relation on $V$.
nodes.title: Finite simple graph

nodes.summary: For finite graphs $H$ and $G$, $H$ is a minor of $G$ when there is a finite sequence $H = G_0, G_1, \dots, G_k = G$ of finite graphs, with $k \ge 0$, such that for each $i < k$, $G_i$ arises from $G_{i+1}$ by one minor step: an isomorphism, the deletion of one vertex, the deletion of one edge, or the contraction of one edge.
nodes.title: Graph minor relation

nodes.summary: For finite graphs $H$ and $G$, $H$ arises from $G$ by one minor step when one of the following holds. Isomorphism: $H$ is isomorphic to $G$. Vertex deletion: for some vertex $a$ of $G$ there is an injective map $f$ from the vertices of $H$ to the vertices of $G$ whose image consists of all vertices other than $a$, such that vertices $u, v$ of $H$ are adjacent exactly when $f(u), f(v)$ are adjacent in $G$. Edge…
nodes.title: One-step graph minor

nodes.summary: For finite graphs $H$ and $G$, if $H$ is isomorphic to $G$, then $H$ is a minor of $G$.
nodes.title: An isomorphic copy is a minor

nodes.summary: For finite graphs $H$ and $G$, if $H$ arises from $G$ by one minor step, then $H$ is a minor of $G$.
nodes.title: A single minor step gives a minor

nodes.summary: Every finite graph $G$ is a minor of itself.
nodes.title: Reflexivity of the graph minor relation

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a family of finite simple graphs that is closed under taking minors: whenever $G \in F$ and $H$ is a minor of $G$, also $H \in F$. Then any two finite graphs that are minors of each other are isomorphic, and there is a finite set $O$ of finite graphs such that a finite graph $G$ belongs to $F$ if and only if no graph in $O$ is a minor of $G$.
nodes.title: Robertson–Seymour theorem

nodes.summary: For finite graphs $H$, $K$ and $G$, if $H$ is a minor of $K$ and $K$ is a minor of $G$, then $H$ is a minor of $G$.
nodes.title: Transitivity of the graph minor relation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
